key_insight: An AI agent can take a prohibited action even when the user’s request is benign and every returned tool statement is true—if a safety-critical fact is missing. EpiSEM-Bench tests how agents handle this evidence gap.
problem_solved: Evaluating whether tool-using agents recognize missing safety evidence, recover needed information, and respect action boundaries rather than treating incomplete information as permission.
method: Introduce an executable benchmark with 300 matched unsafe/safe task pairs across six domains.
Evaluate agents under tool responses that omit safety-relevant facts without making false statements.
Assess unsafe execution, safety boundaries, and evidence recovery.
impact: For practitioners, truthful tool outputs are not enough to ensure safe agent behavior. This benchmark helps evaluate whether agents seek the evidence needed before taking consequential actions.
visual_elements: Decision-flow diagram: benign request → incomplete tool response → recover evidence or risk unsafe action.
Side-by-side matched unsafe/safe scenarios highlighting the safety-critical fact.
Benchmark overview graphic showing 300 task pairs across six domains.
Three evaluation icons: unsafe execution, safety boundaries, and evidence recovery.
paper_title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
paper_authors: Qijin Zhang, Hanzhen Wang, Yuehan Zhao, Haoyu Dai, Yao Shu
